1.explanation: Both the unminified and minified YAML definition files define a “string” pattern whose lookahead only permits end-of-line, comma, or closing bracket/brace after the closing quote. That prevents the regex from matching strings with trailing comments. To fix the highlighting, the lookahead must be extended to allow a '#' (comment) token after the closing quote so Prism still recognizes the string before the comment.
1.bug_scenario: In YAML code blocks, when a quoted string is followed by an inline comment (e.g. - "world" # test), Prism’s YAML grammar fails to recognize the string token because its regex lookahead doesn’t allow comments after the closing quote. As a result, the string and the comment are both unhighlighted (greyed out) instead of the string being highlighted.

2.explanation: The YAML definition in prism-yaml.js declares both a 'string' token and a 'comment' token. The 'comment' pattern (/#.*/ ) indiscriminately grabs any '#' and everything after it, so when a comment appears on the same line as a string literal, the comment rule runs first and swallows the quotes. Meanwhile, the 'string' pattern only matches if the quoted content is immediately followed by end-of-line or structural punctuation—not a '#'. To fix this, the string regex or its placement needs adjusting (for example, using a greedy pattern or reordering so that 'string' is tested before 'comment'), ensuring that quoted strings are recognized even when a comment follows on the same line.
2.bug_scenario: In the provided HTML snippet with a YAML code block, a quoted string that has a comment on the same line (e.g. "world" # test) is not being highlighted as a string. Instead, once the parser hits the “#”, the rest of the line (including the quoted string) is treated as a comment, so the string never gets its own highlighting.
